patterns.content: 兼顾趣味性与历史严谨性 | 稀缺性极强,形成核心技术壁垒;联合考古专家,确保上古音、古蜀方言复原的准确性,搭建专属方言数据库,同类项目难以复制,提升内容独特性.脚本生成 | GPT + 考古资料 + 情感化改写 + 专业文案打磨 | 兼顾专业性与趣味性,避免文化硬科普;结合短视频传播规律,打造有话题、有情感、有传播点的脚本,提升内容互动率与传播效率.剪辑与适配 | 剪映专业版 + 自动字幕/封面 + 多平台适配工具 | 高效批量生产,单条视频剪辑周期缩短至24小时内,降低人力成本;适配多平台内容要求,无需重复剪辑,提升内容分发效率.已验证成果（创赛重点强化）:实验账号「小空没信号」凭借该工作流,仅用15天完成4条视频制作,快速积累1.1万精准粉丝,单条视频自然流量突破100万,互动率达6.2%,远超抖音文旅类账号平均水平（2.5%）,入选抖音精选作者,充分证明工作流的可行性、高效性与适配性.阶段 | 时间周期 | 收入来源 | 核心目标（创赛可量化,突出落地性）

patterns.title: 十一、创赛总结「小空没信号 · 蜀境数字旅人」不是又一个旅行博主,也不是普通的数字人项目,而是四川第...
patterns.content: 十一、创赛总结「小空没信号 · 蜀境数字旅人」不是又一个旅行博主,也不是普通的数字人项目,而是四川第一个、也是目前唯一一个以AI数字人+古蜀文明穿越为核心的文化型文旅IP,更是四川文旅数字化、年轻化升级的重要载体.我们立足四川文旅大省的资源优势,以已充分验证的AIGC创作能力为基础,以“数字人+古蜀文明”为核心竞争力,精准解决省内文旅目的地“内容同质化、数字化薄弱、IP辨识度不足”的核心痛点,构建了“内容引流→B端变现→体验筑壁垒”的完整商业闭环.项目兼具创新性、落地性、盈利性与社会价值:既能够通过AI技术降低文旅宣传成本、提升传播效率,实现商业变现;又能够助力古蜀文明、非遗文化的年轻化传播,推动四川文旅IP升级,契合创赛“创新驱动、产业赋能、文化传承”的核心导向.当前项目已完成技术与流量验证,具备清晰的变现路径与规模化发展潜力,有望快速成为四川数字文旅标杆IP,填补省内文化型数字人文旅IP的市场空白,具备广阔的发展前景与投资价值,恳请评委给予认可与支持.核心亮点（创赛加分重点）:已完成技术与流量验证——实验账号「小空没信号」成功入选抖音精选作者,仅4条AI数字人短视频便快速积累1.

patterns.title: 商务拓展（35%,5
patterns.content: 商务拓展（35%,5.25–7万元）:招聘1名专业商务人员,对接省内文旅客户,加速签约落地;制作客户推介资料,对接2–3家核心意向客户,无需举办大型推介会,控制成本;技术提升（35%,5.25–7万元）:优化数字人形象细节、上古音复原技术,完善AI创作工具,搭建基础内容素材库,将单条视频生产周期从24小时缩短至18小时,提升内容生产效率,无需过度投入技术研发;线下试点（20%,3–4万元）:在1个核心景区（如三星堆博物馆）开展低成本AR导览试点,简化设备投入,积累线下运营经验,为后续规模化拓展奠定基础;流动资金（10%,1.5–2万元）:用于内容制作、基础办公及团队基础薪酬,保障项目冷启动阶段稳步推进,避免资金链断裂.融资回报（创赛加分,贴合实际,不夸大）:预计8–10个月内实现盈亏平衡,18–20个月内收回投资成本,24个月内成为四川数字人文旅细分领域标杆IP,具备规模化复制潜力,为后续融资奠定基础.十、风险与应对全面预判项目推进过程中的潜在风险,结合四川文旅市场实际情况,提出具体、可落地、有针对性的应对方案,体现项目团队的风险意识与应对能力,增强评委对项目可行性的信心.

patterns.title: 目标达成:月收入稳定＞5万元,完成首单交付,客户满意度≥90%,积累1–2个可复制的标杆案例,为下一...
patterns.content: 目标达成:月收入稳定＞5万元,完成首单交付,客户满意度≥90%,积累1–2个可复制的标杆案例,为下一阶段增长奠定基础.八、核心壁垒项目核心壁垒围绕“文化+技术+资源+IP”四大维度构建,区别于普通文旅博主和纯技术类数字人项目,难以被竞争对手复制,是创赛的核心加分项,也是项目长期发展的核心保障.九、融资需求结合项目冷启动阶段核心需求,兼顾创赛“规模化发展”评审导向与初创项目实际,提出低成本、高适配的融资需求,资金用途聚焦核心环节,清晰透明、可量化、可监管,避免冗余投入,确保每一笔资金都能助力项目落地推进.若希望加速商务拓展与团队扩张,提升项目推进速度,适配创赛“规模化发展”评审导向,快速抢占四川数字文旅市场,提出以下融资需求,资金用途清晰、透明,可量化、可监管.融资额:15–20万元（种子轮）;（贴合初创项目规模,降低融资门槛,更具合理性,避免过度融资）融资用途（清晰透明,创赛重点,可量化,聚焦核心需求）:

patterns.title: 第3–4个月:B端突破期（核心:对接客户,建立信任,积累案例）客户对接:组建专项商务团队,带着账号数...
patterns.content: 第3–4个月:B端突破期（核心:对接客户,建立信任,积累案例）客户对接:组建专项商务团队,带着账号数据（粉丝、播放量、互动率）和定制样片,主动拜访/联系广汉市文旅局、三星堆博物馆、金沙遗址博物馆、成都文旅集团等核心客户;敲门动作:提供“免费文旅内容诊断+1条免费定制样片”,降低客户合作门槛,展示项目实力与内容质量;针对不同客户需求,定制专属合作方案;案例积累:完成2–3条免费样片制作,与3–5家潜在客户建立合作意向,整理合作案例手册;目标达成:与3–5家潜在客户建立合作意向,完成2–3条免费样片制作,明确1–2家意向签约客户,完善B端服务流程.第5–6个月:首单落地期（核心:实现变现,验证模式,优化服务）签约转化:推进意向客户签约,签下1–2个正式客户（优先选择中小景区或非遗项目,降低签约难度,快速实现首单落地）;服务交付:按照合作方案,完成定制内容制作、分发与数据复盘,确保客户满意度,打造标杆案例;服务优化:根据客户反馈,优化内容定制流程、配音质量与分发策略,完善数据报告体系;整理“AI文旅工作流”手册,为后续规模化服务做准备;

patterns.title: 结合创赛“阶段性目标”要求,制定清晰、可落地的变现节奏,每个阶段均有明确的收入目标、执行重点与成果导...
patterns.content: 结合创赛“阶段性目标”要求,制定清晰、可落地的变现节奏,每个阶段均有明确的收入目标、执行重点与成果导向,确保项目稳步推进,体现项目的盈利潜力与可持续性.七、冷启动执行计划（6个月,创赛重点:可执行、可落地、有明确动作、有时间节点）聚焦“内容破圈→B端对接→首单落地→模式验证”,制定6个月冷启动计划,每阶段任务明确、动作具体、目标可量化,确保项目快速启动,适配创赛“落地性”评审要求,体现团队的执行能力.第1–2个月:内容锚定期（核心:强化IP标签,积累流量,打造爆款）内容聚焦:集中打造三星堆/古蜀文明系列短视频,每周更新2条,重点突出“数字人穿越+上古音说文物”,强化“古蜀数字人”标签,确保内容专业性与传播性;引流动作:主动@四川文旅、三星堆博物馆、德阳/广汉文旅等官方账号,提交内容合作申请,争取互动转发;参与抖音文旅类话题挑战,借助平台流量破圈;优化迭代:根据视频数据（播放量、互动率）,优化数字人形象与内容风格,形成标准化内容模板;目标达成:粉丝破5万,至少1条视频突破百万播放,单条视频平均互动率≥5%,完成账号IP定位优化,与1–2家博物馆达成初步合作意向.

patterns.title: 文化叙事脚本:基于真实考古资料、历史背景,由专业文案团队打造有情感、有故事、有传播点的脚本,避免生硬...
patterns.content: 文化叙事脚本:基于真实考古资料、历史背景,由专业文案团队打造有情感、有故事、有传播点的脚本,避免生硬宣传,提升内容接受度;多平台分发运营:覆盖抖音、小红书、B站、视频号四大主流平台,根据不同平台传播规律优化内容形式,提供账号运营、评论回复等增值服务,提升曝光与互动;数据复盘报告:每月输出曝光量、互动量、搜索量、线下带动量等核心数据,结合数据优化后续内容,直观呈现服务价值,增强客户粘性.3.参考定价基础版（单条定制视频）:1–3万元（根据视频复杂度、分发渠道调整,适配中小景区及非遗项目,降低合作门槛）;进阶版（月度服务包）:5–10万元（含4条定制视频+多平台分发+月度数据报告,适配文旅局及重点景区的常态化宣传需求）;高端版（年度IP授权+线下活动）:30–50万元（含IP使用权、全年定制内容、线下互动支持,适配核心客户的长期品牌打造需求）.第三层:体验产品「数字人+景区/博物馆沉浸式体验」,将线上内容延伸至线下,打造差异化体验,提升IP粘性与长期竞争力,同时拓展变现渠道,形成“线上引流→线下转化→线上复购”的闭环,构建同类项目难以复制的竞争壁垒.

patterns.title: 🎯 核心目标（创赛可量化,增强说服力）:3个月内账号粉丝破5万,打造至少1条百万播放爆款视频,单条视...
patterns.content: 🎯 核心目标（创赛可量化,增强说服力）:3个月内账号粉丝破5万,打造至少1条百万播放爆款视频,单条视频平均互动率≥5%,成为四川文旅首个破圈的AI数字人IP,为B端合作奠定坚实的流量与品牌基础.第二层:B端服务「数字人文旅内容包」,精准对接四川省内B端客户,提供定制化、一站式文旅内容服务,基于四川市场实际需求定价,性价比高、合作门槛低,可快速实现商业化变现,同时具备规模化复制潜力.1.服务对象核心客户（优先突破）:广汉市文旅局（三星堆属地）、三星堆博物馆、金沙遗址博物馆、成都文旅集团（流量大、需求强,可快速打造标杆案例）;拓展客户（逐步推进）:乐山、阿坝、绵阳等省内各地市文旅局,都江堰、青城山、峨眉山等重点景区,非遗项目、乡村振兴文旅项目（覆盖面广,可实现规模化盈利）.2.服务内容定制化AI数字人短视频:3–5条/月,根据客户需求定制剧情与内容,贴合客户品牌调性,融入当地文化元素,确保内容专业性与传播性;特色配音服务:提供上古音、古蜀方言、情感化配音,结合考古专家指导,确保配音准确性,提升内容独特性与辨识度;

patterns.title: 2万亿元,其中Z世代消费占比达45%,但当前文旅内容呈现形式普遍陈旧,多以“航拍+旁白”的传统模式为...
patterns.content: 2万亿元,其中Z世代消费占比达45%,但当前文旅内容呈现形式普遍陈旧,多以“航拍+旁白”的传统模式为主,缺乏年轻化、互动性、记忆点,难以匹配Z世代的消费偏好,市场存在明显的内容升级缺口.（二）B端核心痛点内容同质化严重:省内多数文旅目的地内容输出千篇一律,缺乏差异化竞争力,难以形成传播破圈,无法有效吸引年轻群体关注;数字化、AI化能力薄弱:多数文旅局、景区缺乏专业的AIGC创作团队与技术储备,无法适配抖音、小红书等主流短视频平台的传播规律,内容传播效率低下;IP辨识度不足:缺乏一个“有情感、有专业、可持续”的数字人代言载体,难以实现品牌长期沉淀,无法形成专属文旅记忆点;落地成本较高:传统文旅宣传依赖线下拍摄、明星代言,成本高、见效慢,中小景区及文旅局难以承担持续的宣传投入.（三）政策与资源支政策层面:四川省、成都市明确将“数字文旅”“AI+文化”纳入重点发展领域,2025–2026年设立专项扶持资金（单个项目最高扶持50万元）,出台《四川省数字文旅发展行动计划》,明确支持数字人、AR/VR等新技术在文旅领域的应用,为项目落地提供坚实的政策保障.

patterns.title: 「小空没信号 · 蜀境数字旅人」创赛商业计划书一、项目名称「小空没信号 · 蜀境数字旅人」备注:突出...
patterns.content: 「小空没信号 · 蜀境数字旅人」创赛商业计划书一、项目名称「小空没信号 · 蜀境数字旅人」备注:突出账号IP核心辨识度,紧扣“数字人+古蜀文旅”双核心,贴合创赛“创新性+落地性”双重导向,简洁易记,便于评委快速捕捉项目核心定位,同时区别于普通文旅IP,强化“穿越叙事”的差异化标签.二、一句话定位以AI数字人“小空”为核心载体,深度融合古蜀文明穿越叙事与AIGC技术,为四川省内文旅目的地（景区、博物馆、文旅局）提供“可批量生产、可情感共鸣、可IP化运营”的新一代数字文旅内容与沉浸式体验服务,打造四川首个、且具有不可复制性的文化型数字人文旅IP,助力四川文旅数字化、年轻化升级.三、市场机会（一）四川文旅市场基础:资源富集,痛点突出,潜力巨大四川作为全国文旅第一梯队省份,文旅资源禀赋得天独厚:拥有三星堆、金沙遗址等世界级古蜀文明IP,都江堰、青城山、九寨沟等5A级景区36家,非遗项目1500余项,蜀道、藏羌彝文化等特色资源兼具文化深度与传播价值.据四川省文旅厅数据显示,2024年四川文旅总收入突破1.

patterns.title: 需要追踪的关键指标· 航海转化率:参加航海实战营的人数 / 付费星球总人数· 交付完成率:完成航海并...
patterns.content: 需要追踪的关键指标· 航海转化率:参加航海实战营的人数 / 付费星球总人数· 交付完成率:完成航海并产出成果的人数 / 参航人数· 接单成功率:通过社群接到项目的人数 / 活跃成员数· 收入中位数:通过社群变现的成员收入中位数· 小白逆袭率:从“未接过任何商业项目”到“完成至少1单交付”的转化率数据面板运营使用· 对外传播:选择性公开“小白逆袭率”等关键指标,作为社群的核心卖点· 对内优化:根据数据调整航海难度、定价、船长选拔标准· 政府汇报:用数据证明社群在解决就业和培育新兴就业形态上的实际成效七、在落地前,先完成一件事整套打法有足够多的细节,但决定它能否跑通的只有一个动作:下个月,由社群发起人亲自带队做完第一期航海实战营.不在观望中反复研究、修正,而是直接跑完一个周期,拿到第一批可观察的结果和样本.只有跑完这一期,才会知道:· 哪种主题的航海更吸引船员· 船长的成本（时间、精力）能否被收益覆盖· 船员最需要的支持到底是什么· 征信记录在实际操作中会遇到什么问题第一期航海实战营不需要完美,只需要完成.

patterns.title: · 产品形态:船长培养计划（定向邀请制）· 内容:从往期航海优秀船员中筛选3-5人,由社群的发起人或...
patterns.content: · 产品形态:船长培养计划（定向邀请制）· 内容:从往期航海优秀船员中筛选3-5人,由社群的发起人或核心成员手把手教如何带队、如何做项目评审· 价值:培养新船长,让航海实战营可以规模化复制· 交付物:独立带队完成一期航海、获得“船长”认证、参与航海收益分成三、内容运营:每天发什么才让人“追着看”生财有术的内容体系有四个板块.参考其结构,我们为成都OPC中心设计四个内容栏目:栏目一:风向标· 更新频率:每周1-2条· 内容:分享最新的AI工具、政策变化、市场机会· 举例:“这周发现一个叫Gamma的AI工具,做PPT效率提升10倍”· 为什么做:让社群成员不落下信息差,也让外部看到社群的信息敏感度栏目二:实战复盘· 更新频率:每期航海结束后集中发布· 内容:项目背景、目标、组队过程、使用工具、踩坑清单、最终成果、收益数据· 举例:《10天帮火锅店用AI做营销素材,复盘全过程》· 为什么做:这是最能证明社群“实战能力”的内容栏目三:组队日志· 更新频率:不定期· 内容:记录一个项目组队的故事——两个人怎么认识、为什么决定合作、合作过程中发生了什么

patterns.title: · 传播价值:展示长期价值,为续费做铺垫· 采集方式:每季度整理一次,做成员成长追踪二、产品化路径:...
patterns.content: · 传播价值:展示长期价值,为续费做铺垫· 采集方式:每季度整理一次,做成员成长追踪二、产品化路径:把“逆袭”变成可售卖的服务线用户进群后需要清晰知道自己该做什么、怎么一步步完成逆袭.我们用“启航”—“深航”—“领航”三级产品线解决问题.L1:启航计划——从“看”到“做”的第一步· 产品形态:7天体验营（免费或9.9元）· 内容:由一位有经验的OPC带队,完成一个极简单的AI小项目（如“用AI生成你的第一张专属头像/名片”）· 价值:让参与者在7天内亲手完成一件作品并收获认可,打破心理障碍· 转化钩子:体验营最后一天,“如果你想继续做更难但可以赚钱的真项目,我们在付费星球等你”L2:深航计划——从“做”到“赚”的关键一跃· 产品形态:21天付费航海实战营（定价299-499元/期）· 内容:围绕一个真实商业场景（如“AI+餐饮营销”）,由船长带队,5-8人组队,21天内完成一个真实可交付的项目· 价值:每位学员获得项目履历+征信加分,项目成果进入社群案例库· 交付物:项目交付物、个人征信记录增量、正式加入“OPC人才库”L3:领航计划——从“赚”到“带人赚”的生态裂变

patterns.title: 主角C:卡在瓶颈的单干老手· 初期状态:能接单、能交付,但月收入卡在2-3万上不去,因为一个人只能做...
patterns.content: 主角C:卡在瓶颈的单干老手· 初期状态:能接单、能交付,但月收入卡在2-3万上不去,因为一个人只能做这么多事· 逆袭触发:在社群里带了两期航海实战营,培养出3个靠谱的徒弟,把执行端分出去· 逆袭结果:从“自己做”变成“带人做”,月收入翻倍,开始接更大的项目· 情绪钩子:“我以为我的上限是技术,其实我的上限是没找到能托付的人.”2.四类故事素材,长期吸引目标人群素材一:作业打卡· 内容:成员每日在航海实战营打卡,晒出当日成果或操作疑问· 传播价值:展示社群活跃度· 采集方式:运营每天精选3-5条打卡,做成合集发到小红书/朋友圈素材二:阶段性成果复盘· 内容:成员完成每个阶段的复盘· 传播价值:展示“逆袭”的渐变过程,让未加入的人看到路径是真实的· 采集方式:航海实战营结束后,由船长或优秀船员撰写,社群协助排版发布素材三:里程碑事件· 内容:成员首次完成一份完整商业交付,或者某次组队项目的结果和最终收益· 传播价值:展示社群产出的真实商业价值,是最强的内容资产· 采集方式:社群主动采访当事人,记录项目背景、组队过程、交付成果素材四:量变到质变· 内容:成员加入X周/X月后的变化对比

patterns.title: 小白逆袭”叙事延展:让口号变成可复制的商业引擎前面我们已经把三大飞轮的战略框架搭好了
patterns.content: 小白逆袭”叙事延展:让口号变成可复制的商业引擎前面我们已经把三大飞轮的战略框架搭好了.现在,我们深入到每一个环节,把“小白逆袭”从一句口号,变成可以每天执行的标准化动作.一、“小白逆袭”的叙事体系:讲故事的人与故事素材1.三大故事主角,覆盖不同的“逆袭前”状态主角A:卡在门槛外的小白· 初期状态:被AI信息淹没,买了很多课但一个项目都没做成,觉得自己“不是搞技术的料”· 逆袭触发:加入社群后,被塞进一个航海实战营当“水手”,船长手把手带着做完第一个AI项目· 逆袭结果:第一次收到甲方转账（哪怕只有500块）,第一次做出可以放进作品集的东西· 情绪钩子:“不是我不行,是我一直没找到对的入口和带我走的人.”主角B:会技术但不会卖的闷头人· 初期状态:会用Midjourney、会跑ComfyUI,但不知道怎么找客户,接的永远是朋友介绍的500块友情单· 逆袭触发:在社群里被匹配到一个会谈客户但缺执行能力的OPC,两人组队接了一个完整项目· 逆袭结果:第一次收到5位数的项目款,第一次有了“分工协作”的体感· 情绪钩子:“我以为我要学会销售才能接单,结果找到一个会销售的人就够了.”

patterns.title: · 激励机制:精华帖作者获得“成都OPC中心·传道者”称号、下一期航海实战优先报名权、社群官方推荐接...
patterns.content: · 激励机制:精华帖作者获得“成都OPC中心·传道者”称号、下一期航海实战优先报名权、社群官方推荐接单的机会2.建立“OPC征信体系”· 记录什么:每个成员在社群中的实战履历——参加了哪期航海、担任什么角色、获得了什么评价、交付了什么成果· 怎么用:当外部企业找人时,征信档案是比“自我介绍”更有说服力的信任凭证· 对外价值:一个成员的征信档案比任何简历都可信,因为每个条目都有真实项目背书3.封装“OPC成功案例库”· 案例格式:不是“我用AI做了一个视频”,而是完整的商业故事——“遇到了什么问题 → 怎么用AI解决的 → 带来了什么结果”,附上成本和协作流程· 持续更新:每月从精华帖和航海实战中精选3-5个案例,加入案例库· 对外价值:案例库是社群对外报价的底气,也是吸引新成员的广告为什么这样做:生财有术2600多篇精华帖和《生财日历》,本质上就是把“一次性的项目经验”变成了“可以反复售卖的资产”.成都OPC中心要做的就是把12个共创项目、每周的知识分享、每期航海实战的成果都变成“活的案例”,让沉淀内容本身成为引流和转化的利器.联动逻辑:

patterns.title: 优秀船员分享经验,产生真实案例沉淀到知识星球3
patterns.content: 优秀船员分享经验,产生真实案例沉淀到知识星球3.建立“项目组队广场”· 在知识星球或社群中创建需求&技能发布区· 格式:【需求】 描述 + 预算 + 【技能缺口】 描述· 长期开放,让需求持续流动为什么这样做:小白逆袭需要的是一个低门槛、有领队、有明确产出的实战环境.生财有术的大航海计划,每期筛选出船长带队,让船员在真实项目中边做边学,最终产出可验证的成果——这种模式把“逆袭”从口号变成了可复制的生产线.飞轮三:资产沉淀——把“逆袭故事”变成“商业资产”参考依据:生财有术每月有1500多位圈友贡献3000多篇优质内容,其中精华帖约100篇,每篇精华帖平均获得1万+人次阅读.这些精华帖不是“心得体会汇总”,而是真实的项目复盘和方法论.精华帖作者还能获得“传术师”称号和奖励.具体打法:1.建立“OPC精华帖”筛选机制· 不是什么帖都能叫精华:必须满足以下至少2个条件:有真实项目产出、有可复用的方法论、有踩坑复盘、有商业成果数据· 评选流程:成员自荐/推荐 → 运营团队初筛 → 核心评审团（5位发起人轮值）终审

patterns.title: 生财有术最值得借鉴的机制就是“大航海计划”
patterns.content: 生财有术最值得借鉴的机制就是“大航海计划”.参考依据:生财有术的大航海计划,筛选社群里在某个领域最有实战经验的圈友担任船长,全程把握整体方向,推动项目进展.船员需要提交申请,介绍自身情况,筛选出最适合一起并肩作战的人.具体打法:1.发起“OPC航海实战营”· 频率:每两周或每月一期,每期一个主题· 主题来源:从社群12个共创项目中提炼,或根据成员兴趣发起· 举例:《10天,用AI为1家线下实体店做全套营销素材》《7天,用AI帮1个乡村民宿生成全套宣传内容》· 船长角色:由社群内在该方向有实战经验的OPC担任,负责设定方向、指导执行、评审成果· 船员招募:公开报名,提交申请（我能做什么、我想学什么、每天可投入几小时）,由船长筛选· 围观机制:落选者可进入围观群,同步观察、参与讨论2.航海实战的标准化流程· 第1天:开营仪式.船长发布项目背景和需求说明,船员做自我介绍和技能匹配· 第2-3天:船长发布实战手册（参考生财有术的航海实战手册模式）,船员开始执行· 第4-8天:每日打卡汇报进展,船长在群内点评指导· 第9天:提交成果,船长和社群内相关领域专家评审· 第10天:闭营复盘.

patterns.title: · 内容积累:每周专业知识分享、AI创意接龙、线下工作坊借鉴生财有术,将这些资产系统化、产品化、可复...
patterns.content: · 内容积累:每周专业知识分享、AI创意接龙、线下工作坊借鉴生财有术,将这些资产系统化、产品化、可复制化,是这套打法战略的核心.二、打法战略:三大飞轮驱动“小白逆袭”生态飞轮一:价值筛选——用付费筛出“认真的人”参考依据:生财有术初期采用低初始定价（365元）,然后梯度涨价,每满100人涨价100元,营造紧迫感.当前年费近2000元,仍有数万会员持续付费,证明了“定价即筛选”的有效性.具体打法:1.推出知识星球付费社群· 年费定价为399-599元,首批早鸟价更低,随人数增加逐步涨价· 定价逻辑:足够筛选出愿意投入的人,又不至于吓退刚起步的OPC小白2.梯度涨价机制· 每满50人或每月调价一次,给观望者紧迫感· 老会员续费享受折扣价（参考生财有术的老会员续费8折模式）3.72小时无条件退款· 降低决策门槛,让用户敢于尝试· 同时倒逼前3天的交付质量为什么这样做:生财有术的实践证明,付费社群的核心价值不是“收了多少钱”,而是“筛出了什么样的人”.愿意付费的人,本身就是有执行力、愿意投资自己的人.这是整个飞轮启动的前提.飞轮二:实战激活——用“航海”驱动“逆袭”这是整个战略的核心引擎.

.我帮你逐层拆解,然后说一说,放到你的“成都OPC中心”里,应该怎么看、怎么用.一、什么是OPC的“中台思路”?她说的“中台”,不是让你去开发一套软件卖钱,而是指把你们社群运作中积累的、可以复用的东西,沉淀成一个能持续产生价值的中间层,而不是停留在一个个散点的项目上.结合你们现有的资产,“中台”可以具象化为三个东西:1.一套“可售卖的知识资产”· 不只是“软件变知识库”,而是你们的实战方法论.比如“OPC如何两两组队”、“如何探索并验证一个细分需求”、“一个AI+乡村振兴项目从0到1的复盘手册”.· 变现方式:整理成付费报告、课程、轻咨询.你们已经跑通的12个项目,每一个都是一份可以卖钱的避坑指南.2.一个“可复用的协作网络”· 你们300人的信任关系、技能标签库、项目组队机制,这本身就是一个庞大的中台.· 变现方式:不是靠群主一个一个撮合,而是把网络的能力（比如“快速组建一个AI视频团队”）封装成标准服务,卖给需要短期、高强度、高信任协作的外部企业或机构.3.一种“可放大的信任背书”· 你们已经有的“成都社造大会”分享等,就是一种信任中台.

patterns.title: 周子懿（周玥）企业级AI Agent定制开发及AI应用产品累计变现70万元,擅长从行业真实痛点切入,...
patterns.content: 周子懿（周玥）企业级AI Agent定制开发及AI应用产品累计变现70万元,擅长从行业真实痛点切入,在不改变现有工作逻辑的前提下,以最小业务闭环帮助企业完成数字化转型,企业级AI落地交付.辛酉时居文化发展有限公司法人,世界劳工组织人工智能大师认证,中国产学研合作促进会会员,亚洲经贸研究院经贸委员会委员,成都理工大学砚湖企业家俱乐部人工智能专委会理事,成都OPC中心联合发起人,四川省企业发展促进中心“AI·OPC赋能企业突围实战训练”首期分享嘉宾.为什么做这件事传统AI服务的问题在于:技术团队不懂行业语言,企业不敢推翻既有流程.我的差异在于同时具备商业判断与技术交付能力——拆解行业真实痛点,用轻量Agent完成最小闭环.已落地项目覆盖文旅、乡村振兴、跨境电商、海洋渔业、市场调研等垂直领域,典型交付包括:乡村振兴整村治理及文旅打卡营销Agent与小程序;田野调查数据清洗、知识图谱构建与可视化看板小程序;文旅女性历史角色情绪交互Agent;海洋气象海事及渔情分析Agent（融合资深渔民经验）.

patterns.title: 分别卡在哪里?在座的企业如果现在要动,第一步应该做什么?对校友企业之间互相借力,三位有什么建议?3
patterns.content: 分别卡在哪里?在座的企业如果现在要动,第一步应该做什么?对校友企业之间互相借力,三位有什么建议?3.资源亮底（30 分钟）每人 1.5 分钟,三块内容:我是谁、核心能力;能给什么资源;想链接什么资源.主持人只做复述和关键词提炼,帮全场记住关键信息,不发散、不追问.4.全体开放式探讨（45 分钟）围绕三个问题自然展开:①论坛中提到的情况,在场各位有什么实际体感?②手头的资源和卡点,有什么可以互相借力的地方?③如果要一起做点事情,从哪里切入最可行?主持人把控节奏、引导但不主讲,鼓励企业家之间互相提问和回应.5.共识提炼（15 分钟）由主持人收束,对当天探讨的卡点与思路做总结,三块内容:①核心卡点——讨论中梳理出的主要卡点与成因;②共性思路——交流中形成的解决思路、可复用经验与可调用资源;③下一步——纪要发布与跟进安排.6.会长总结收尾（5 分钟）总结收尾,内容由会长自定.八、组织分工（建议）以下为建议分工,具体人选与职责由俱乐部商定后确认.九、会前准备（一周内倒排）十、物资清单《资源清单》打印成册 25 份《卡点汇总》打印 25 份圆桌论坛问题提纲（打印给主持人）

patterns.title: 供参考的大致方向:技术 / 产品方、行业应用 / 需求方、渠道与园区资源方、资本与专业服务等各方向邀...
patterns.content: 供参考的大致方向:技术 / 产品方、行业应用 / 需求方、渠道与园区资源方、资本与专业服务等各方向邀请若干位,构成可灵活.五、会前问卷与两份材料5.1 问卷收集（随邀请函当天发出,活动前 2–3 天回收完毕）——每位参会者须提交:5.2 会前输出两份材料——让会议一开场就有抓手,不用大家现场现想:《资源清单》:汇总所有参会者的「要什么 + 给什么」,每人一栏,打印成册,现场发放;《卡点汇总》:匿名整理所有卡点,归为 3–4 类,作为共同探讨环节的话题素材.六、活动流程（议程）14:00–16:30 共 150 分钟.论坛嘉宾角度与话题方向详见第七章;如需安排茶歇,可在第四段前顺延 10 分钟.七、关键环节说明1.会长致辞（10 分钟）开场致辞,内容由会长自定.2.圆桌论坛（45 分钟）论坛由 1 位主持人 + 3 位嘉宾构成.主持人负责提问引导,不主讲;3 位嘉宾从三个不同角度分享,避免单一视角.嘉宾角度与人选由主办方邀请确定,以下为参考框架:话题方向（主持人提前准备问题提纲,以下供参考）:从各自角度看,企业做 AI 与数字化转型,现在最真实的现状是什么?最常见的坑有哪些?

patterns.title: 活动策划方案 · 标准版成都理工大学砚湖企业俱乐部「AI 与 OPC 生态」闭门座谈会圆桌论坛 · ...
patterns.content: 活动策划方案 · 标准版成都理工大学砚湖企业俱乐部「AI 与 OPC 生态」闭门座谈会圆桌论坛 · 资源亮底 · 共同探讨 —— 20 人 / 约 2.5 小时,正式、高效、有产出一、活动背景砚湖企业俱乐部拟推进 OPC 引入园区及 OPC 孵化工作.校友企业中相当一部分从事 AI 与 OPC 相关业务,供需互补明显,但彼此缺乏系统化的互通渠道.为此,拟组织一场以圆桌论坛、资源亮底、共同探讨为核心的闭门座谈会:先由不同角度的嘉宾分享行业认知与实践,再梳理校友企业间的供需资源,并围绕共性卡点展开集体探讨,推动合作意向落地.二、活动定位与会议纪律活动形式:正式闭门座谈会,20 人,约 2.5 小时.非工作坊、非培训、非路演.活动风格:正式、高效、有产出.核心逻辑:先统一认知、再亮出资源、最后共同探讨.全程三件事——①听不同角度的真实分享,建立判断框架;②让大家知道谁有谁缺;③让大家针对卡点和资源自然对话.三、活动基本信息四、参会名单说明参会名单以定向邀请为主,实际构成依邀请与报名情况而定,不作固定比例要求.

patterns.title: 4 / 把 AI 沙盘包装成"AI 预测爆款"沙盘是过滤器不是预测器
patterns.content: 4 / 把 AI 沙盘包装成"AI 预测爆款"沙盘是过滤器不是预测器.对外承诺收益、对内把 AI 结论当决策依据,都会在第一次失准时摧毁信任.定位永远是:AI 筛掉明显错的,真金白银的市集数据才是裁判.参考资料本文引用的外部案例与数据来源[1] ZOO GROUP · NSC 自然共生社区官网 —nsclife.cn（ZOO 集团业务与自孵化子线信息）[2] Pokemon GO 地标打卡机制参考 —pokemongolive.com[3] 支付宝集五福 / 蚂蚁森林养成机制参考 —alipay.com[4] THE BOX 朝外（北京,策展型年轻力商业,近 300 位主理人合作）—theboxchaowai.com[5] 艾媒咨询:2025 年中国情绪经济市场规模约 2.7 万亿元,预计 2029 年超 4.5 万亿 —iimedia.cn[6] 中国政府网:青年就业创业政策相关文件 —gov.cn口径说明各 AI 结合点的"真实价值/前提/风险"为基于公开技术与行业经验的判断,落地前需以真实使用数据验证;成本与收益测算为量级估计.ZOO GROUP 为对标借鉴案例,非本项目合作方.

patterns.title: 内容流水线 + 预售认养开摊前先攒粉丝和订单,品牌带势能进场→线下验货市集实销 + 打卡传播销售数据...
patterns.content: 内容流水线 + 预售认养开摊前先攒粉丝和订单,品牌带势能进场→线下验货市集实销 + 打卡传播销售数据实时回流,拍照助手放大传播→AI 裁决数据闸门判定晋级晋级快闪/慢闪,留观迭代,淘汰复盘→放大发行升级包 + 坪效 + 成绩单开店、对接渠道基金、或被收编为蘑菇子线循环二 · 消费者循环:逛一次 → 养成 → 陪品牌长大 → 带新人来第一次来被内容/精灵吸引线上种草或朋友分享,来逛市集→参与养成捕捉精灵 / 认养品牌 / 投票消费、打卡、投票决定新品,AI 周报维持连接→看到成长精灵进化 / 品牌晋级品牌从市集升快闪,精灵全社区进化——情感绑定形成→传播带新拍照助手 + 社交裂变分享打卡内容、晒稀有精灵,带新用户进场两个循环怎么咬合品牌需要消费者参与养成（预售、投票提供需求信号）;消费者需要品牌晋级（精灵进化、认养回报提供情感收益）.中间靠 AI 数据中台把两者的每一次互动都变成数据——品牌数据进评审官,消费者数据进会员体系.这就是"青年社区"而不只是"孵化工厂"的原因:孵化是过程,社区是让过程被看见、被参与、被分享的场.六、落地顺序:按"价值 × 难度"排,先磨刀后砍柴

patterns.title: 创意同质化——AI 管执行、人管创意,分工要明确结论能成,效率工具,P2 上
patterns.content: 创意同质化——AI 管执行、人管创意,分工要明确结论能成,效率工具,P2 上.AI 子品牌孵化器环7 · 发行 · 战略级机制:蘑菇自有子线（MOOCOOL COFFEE、蘑菇文创等）立项前先过 AI 沙盘 → 市集验证 → 数据达标才开实体.外部孵化品牌毕业时,AI 自动生成"品牌成绩单"（全周期数据报告）对接渠道与基金真实价值这是借鉴 ZOO 的最终落点:ZOO 用重资产孵化子线,蘑菇用"AI 沙盘 + 市集数据 + 自有流水线"轻资产孵化子线.每条子线的立项验证成本从"开店试错（数十万）"降到"沙盘 + 3 个月市集（几千到几万）".成绩单同时解决外部品牌的"毕业去处"——数据是新的信用前提条件前六环跑通才有意义:沙盘、评审官、数据中台都是它的前置风险子线扩张稀释母品牌——严格过三道闸（沙盘→市集→数据）再开实体,宁可慢结论战略级,放最后.前六环是磨刀,这一环是砍柴——刀磨好了自然有柴.五、线上线下融合:两个循环互相咬合品牌循环（孵化业务）+ 消费者循环（社区养成）,靠数据中台咬在一起循环一 · 品牌循环:线上攒势能 → 线下验货 → AI 裁决 → 放大线上养成

patterns.title: 触达骚扰感——邀约文案要个性化（用对方账号内容做钩子）,别群发结论能成,但合规先行
patterns.content: 触达骚扰感——邀约文案要个性化（用对方账号内容做钩子）,别群发结论能成,但合规先行.P3 上,先人工+AI 半自动跑通再全自动.AI 客流动线 · 坪效分析环6 · 放大机制:摄像头/收银数据 → 摊位热力图 → AI 每周给布局建议（谁该挪到哪、哪些品类相邻能互相导流）真实价值摊位位置显著影响销售额（行业经验 30–50% 差距）.动态调摊位直接增收,而且"AI 排摊"本身就是对主理人的公平承诺——位置好坏不再靠关系前提条件硬件投入（摄像头/动线传感器）+ 隐私合规（数据脱敏、告知）风险动线数据不足时结论不可靠;硬件成本要跟点位收入匹配结论能成,属于"有实体点位后再投"的能力.P3 做,先用收银数据 + 人工观察过渡.AI 活动策划助手环3 / 环4机制:周/月/季活动体系的内容生成——主题、玩法、物料清单、预算预估、传播文案一键产出,人工把关创意方向真实价值策展人力是蘑菇的固定成本.AI 把"每场活动 60% 的重复工作"（物料清单、文案、排期）自动化,活动密度能上去——而内容活动供给正是复访的关键前提条件12 年活动档案就是训练素材（主题、玩法、物料、预算都有现成数据）风险

patterns.title: 结论页面级能成,直播级观望
patterns.content: 结论页面级能成,直播级观望.P2 做页面级.4.3 给蘑菇自己的五个工具（平台层）AI 晋级评审官环5 · 裁决机制:六步漏斗每步定义硬指标（销售额、复购率、社群增长、内容数据、预售达成率）,AI 自动汇总判定"晋级/留观/淘汰",人只审例外真实价值把"人情评审"变"数据评审",标准可复制是 Park 从 1 个点位复制到 10 个城市的前提;对主理人而言规则透明反而更有信任感前提条件指标阈值需要 2–3 场市集数据校准,先"人判为主、AI 辅助",跑稳后翻转风险唯数据论会误杀"慢热型"品牌——保留申诉通道,人审例外制度化结论能成,是平台的地基.P2 上线,先双轨并行.AI 招商雷达环1 · 发现机制:扫描小红书/抖音/闲鱼上的潜力新品牌与新主理人 → LLM 分类打分（审美/社群/内容能力）→ 自动建档 → 主动邀约入驻真实价值把供给从"3000+ 存量名单"变成"全网活水";招商成本从人肉拜访降到自动发现 + 主动触达.对平台而言,优质供给的持续输入比流量更重要前提条件数据抓取需处理平台合规（优先用合规 API 与公开内容,避免爬虫红线）风险

patterns.content: 平台孵化的外部品牌拿"AI 成绩单"对接渠道与基金.这环是借鉴 ZOO 的关键落点,见下一章.一句话定义这条流水线线下版是"人肉漏斗":每一环靠人力推进,数据是副产品.AI 原生版是"数据漏斗":每一环的 AI 工具既是生产者也是数据收集器——沙盘产模拟数据、内容流水线产传播数据、市集产销售数据、养成互动产会员数据,全部回流喂养下一环的 AI.孵化越跑越多,漏斗越磨越锋利,这就是 Park 的护城河.二、借鉴 ZOO:它的孵化逻辑,映射成 Park 的四个设计原则ZOO 是对标对象:一个母体世界观孵出 20+ 子线.蘑菇要借鉴的是逻辑,不是重资产路线.ZOO 的孵化逻辑ZOO 是怎么做的映射到 Park 流水线的哪一环母体世界观所有子线长在"人与自然和谐共生"一个价值观上:咖啡、酒店、营地、公益共享同一套叙事环2 筛选 + 环3 养成:AI 品牌教练输出的所有品牌方案统一挂在"青年生活美学/让热爱变成生意"的蘑菇母叙事下——子线再散,讲的是同一个故事品类延伸

patterns.content: 验证（Validate）—— 线下市集验货线下版:销售数据靠人工登记,卖得好不好全凭感觉AI 版:收银/扫码数据实时回流 →AI 经营日报每天告诉主理人"今天什么卖得好、明天该带什么";AI 选品补货按天气/节假日/周边活动预测备货.同时 AI 拍照助手把消费者的打卡变成品牌的传播.5裁决（Judge）—— 数据说话线下版:晋级靠人情、靠主观印象,标准不可复制AI 版:AI 晋级评审官按六步漏斗（市集验证→快闪→慢闪→旗舰→内容IP→投资）的硬指标自动判定晋级/留观/淘汰,人只审例外.公平的标准才能规模化复制.6放大（Scale）—— 开店与坪效线下版:晋级的品牌各凭本事,街区运营靠经验拍脑袋AI 版:AI 品牌升级包（VI/门头/包装一键重做）+AI 客流动线坪效分析（热力图→摊位/铺位布局持续优化,位置直接影响销售额）.7发行（Launch）—— 毕业去处线下版:品牌孵完就散,没有自己的渠道,没有"母品牌"沉淀AI 版:AI 子品牌孵化器.蘑菇自己的子线（MOOCOOL COFFEE、蘑菇文创……）走同一条流水线:沙盘→市集→数据达标→开实体.

patterns.title: MooCoolPark:AI 原生青年品牌孵化流水线MooCoolPark · 策略研究稿 v3（A...
patterns.content: MooCoolPark:AI 原生青年品牌孵化流水线MooCoolPark · 策略研究稿 v3（AI 原生版）把孵化流水线用 AI 重造一遍蘑菇过去做的是线下版:找人靠人脉、筛人靠眼缘、试错靠真金白银、运营靠一人多岗.这版不讨论画像、不讨论常识,只回答一件事:如果把这条流水线的每一环都换成 AI + 数据驱动,它会变成什么样;每一个 AI 结合点,到底能不能成、省的是什么、需要什么前提.7环AI 原生孵化流水线15个AI 结合点逐一评估12年数据底座（AI 的原料壁垒）3期按"价值×难度"排序落地先给结论:AI 原生流水线的四个根本变化1 / 从"人肉漏斗"变成"数据漏斗"传统孵化的每一环都靠人的经验和体力,所以慢、贵、不可复制.AI 原生流水线的每一环都在生产数据:数据喂养 AI,AI 替掉重复劳动,人只做创造和例外判断.孵化做得越多,漏斗磨得越锋利——这才是平台生意的复利.2 / 从"先开店再试错"变成"先模拟再验证"线下版的试错成本是摊位费 + 备货 + 时间（一场市集至少 2000–5000 元 + 一周）.

patterns.content: 本人毕业于传播科学与艺术学院,始终对母校怀有深厚感情.经过数年产业实践,已在高校 孵化、乡村OPC、非遗+AI、跨境文化出海四个方向上积累了可复用的方法论与实战资源. 其中,「启程」OPC孵化机制、AI智能体技术及非遗+AI产品落地经验与学校当前的人才培 养、非遗培训及创新创业教育工作高度契合. 本人不追求头衔,而希望以理事身份为平台,将已跑通的能力与资源系统性地对母校开放. 无论本次申请是否通过,本人均愿意持续为学校及校友贡献价值. 恳请协会领导与各位老师予以考虑. 此致 敬礼 申请人:周玥 2018届传播科学与艺术学院 · 环境设计专业 2026年5月20日 成都

patterns.title: 相关产品已投放市场,销售反馈良好,验证了AI驱动非遗创新的商业化闭环
patterns.content: 相关产品已投放市场,销售反馈良好,验证了AI驱动非遗创新的商业化闭环.在此基础上,本人具备从文化转译 → AI辅助设计 → B端交付的完整能力,并已与82位签约非遗传承人建立供应链合作关系.（四）跨境文化出海与AI技术能力跨境独立站选品及文化转译实战经验企业级定制Agent开发、AI供需对接系统搭建北京某央企跨境出海选品师实战背景三、对学校的价值贡献本人充分了解成都理工大学开设有传播科学与艺术学院开设有非遗研修培训项目（面向校外非遗人培训）,并愿为此提供实质性赋能.本人承诺在以下方面支持学校工作:（一）为非遗创新培训班提供AI赋能教学支持

patterns.title: （一）「启程」OPC订单式孵化引擎——高校学生创新创业与就业解决方案该平台的核心定位为:以项目制方式...
patterns.content: （一）「启程」OPC订单式孵化引擎——高校学生创新创业与就业解决方案该平台的核心定位为:以项目制方式,帮助高校学生实现从学习者到经营者的转化.具体模式为:采用订单式、项目制孵化路径,学生在真实业务中完成能力构建孵化目标为OPC一人公司或小规模公司,具备独立承接业务与自我造血能力,平台已入驻成都数据集团·蓉数产业生态,拥有政府级数据与产业通道支撑,该模式已跑通并具备可复制性.本人愿将该孵化机制优先引入母校,直接服务于在校学生的创新创业与高质量就业.（二）乡村OPC——以能力建设赋能乡村数字化转型乡村OPC与订单式孵化在逻辑上有所区分,其重点不在于订单对接,而在于通过OPC能力建设,解决乡村实际运营问题.当前正在温江等地推进,具体方向包括:民宿数据沉淀:协助乡村民宿建立数据采集、分析与运营体系,整村运营支持:利用数字化手段服务乡村资源整合与运营决策在地人才培养:面向新村民、手工艺人等开展OPC能力建设（三）非遗创新与AI产品落地——已实现市场化验证本人利用AI技术,独立完成非遗产品的设计转化与落地,主要面向B端客户提供非遗主题包装解决方案（如礼盒设计、文化IP包装等）.

patterns.title: The search strategy was structured around five cor...
patterns.content: The search strategy was structured around five core concepts: (1) clinical artificial intelligence(including artificial intelligence, machine learning, deep learning, neural networks, and large language models such as ChatGPT/GPT); (2) explicit patient, family, or public perspectives; (3) healthcare and clinical contexts; (4) AI use or implementation in care; and(5) empirical data collection methods. Searches required explicit mention of AI technologies in the title or abstract and included only studies reporting primary datacollected through qualitative, quantitative, or mixed-methods designs (e.g., surveys, interviews, focus groups, cross-sectional orobservational studies).To maintain focus on AI as the object of perception rather than a background analytic tool, studies centeredon telehealth were excluded. Systematic reviews, scoping reviews, narrative reviews, and other literature-only reviews were alsoexcluded at the search level using title and abstract text exclusions.Search strategies were adapted to the indexing and field structures of each database, including the use of MeSH terms in PubMedand Emtree terms in Embase, with database-specific refinements applied to ensure consistent conceptual alignment.All retrieved records were subsequently screened at the title/abstract and full-text levels to confirm eligibility.Included papers were tagged byclinical specialty and geographic representation by four reviewers.To facilitate visualization, tags were res-structured as binaryvariables using Claude (Sonnet 4.6), and outputs were manually reviewed for accuracy.Mock figures were generated using Claude410

patterns.title: This metric identifies the fastest growing occupat...
patterns.content: This metric identifies the fastest growing occupations within each AI talent segment by country, based on year-over-year changes inoccupation share.For each occupation, LinkedIn calculates the year-over-year growth rate as the percentage change in the share ofmembers listing an AI occupation compared with the same month one year earlier.Sample interpretation: In the United States, AI product manager is among the fastest growing occupations within the AI engineering segment, showing the largest year-over-year increase.10.AI Skills Diffusion IndexThe AI skills diffusion index measures the breadth and depth of adoption of AI skills across the LinkedIn member base.It capturesboth (i) how widespread a given group of AI skills is among members in a country and (ii) how diverse the set of AI skills representedon member profiles is within that group.The index is constructed by tracking the share of members who list at least one AI skill on402 APPENDIX | AI INDEX REPORT 2026their profile, adjusted for the diversity of distinct AI skills observed in a given country.Values are indexed relative to a baseline periodwhere a member threshold is reached at the country level, which ensures stability and comparability across countries and over time.The resulting index value at any point in the time series reflects how much the adjusted share of members with that AI skill group hasincreased relative to the baseline. Because the index is normalized to an early reference point, it is best interpreted as a measure ofgrowth in diffusion rather than as a level or penetration rate.Sample interpretation: In the United States, the AI skills diffusion index for AI engineering indicates that the adjusted share ofmembers listing AI literacy skills is 1075x higher than it was in March 2023.Acknowledgments

patterns.title: LinkedIn data provides insights to countries on AI...
patterns.content: LinkedIn data provides insights to countries on AI talent gained or lost due to migration trends.AI talent migration is considered for allmembers with AI skills/holding AI jobs at time “t” for country A as the country of interest and country B as the source of inflows anddestination for outflows.Net AI talent migration between country A and country B would therefore be calculated as:Net flows are defined as total arrivals minus departures within a given time period. LinkedIn membership varies between countries,making it a challenge to interpret absolute movements of members from one country to another.Migration flows are thereforenormalized with respect to each country.For example, for country A, all absolute net flows into and out of country A, regardlessof origin and destination countries, are normalized based on the LinkedIn membership of country A at the end of each year andmultiplied by 10,000. Hence, this metric indicates relative talent migration from all countries to and from country A.Note: Minimumthresholds have been applied to ensure that transitions have a sufficient sample size.Sample interpretation: The United States had a positive net flow of AI talent relative to its membership size at 1.07 net flow per10,000 members.8.Career Transitions into AI JobsLinkedIn considers the source occupations that feed AI occupations, analyzing the share of transitions into AI occupations pooled over a five-year period.Career transitions are computed by aggregating member-leveljob transitions from one occupation to another occupation that the member has previously not held.LinkedInexcludes first occupations added by new graduates and intra-occupation transitions.Sample interpretation: In the United States, 26.9% of transitions into AI engineer came from software engineer, followed by 13.3%from data scientist.9.Fastest Growing AI Occupations

patterns.title: Sample interpretation: A country’s relative AI ski...
patterns.content: Sample interpretation: A country’s relative AI skills penetration rate of 2 in the education sector means the average penetration of AIskills in that country is two times the global average across the same set of occupations in that sector.Global Comparison: By GenderThe relative AI skills penetration by gender provides a cross-country comparison of AI skills penetrations within401 APPENDIX | AI INDEX REPORT 2026a gender.Since the global averages are distinct for each gender, this metric should only be used to comparecountry rankings within each gender, not for cross-gender comparisons within countries.Sample interpretation: If a country’s AI skills penetration for women is 1.5, that means members who are women in that country are1.5x more likely to list AI skills than the average female member in all countries pooled together across the same set of occupations that exist in the country-gender combination.Global Comparison: Across GendersThe relative AI skills penetration across genders allows for cross-gender comparisons within and acrosscountries globally, since LinkedIn compares a country’s AI skills penetration by gender to the same global averageregardless of gender.6.Female Representation in AIThe share of AI talent that are women.Sample interpretation: Female representation within AI talent with AI engineering skills is 30.5% globally.7. AI Talent MigrationData on migration comes from the World Bank Group–LinkedIn “Digital Data for Development” partnership (see https://linkedindata.worldbank.org/ and Zhu et al.(2018)).LinkedIn migration rates are derived from the self-identified locations of LinkedIn memberprofiles.For example, when a LinkedIn member updates their location from Paris to London, this is counted as a migration.Migrationdata is available from 2019 on.

patterns.title: • LinkedIn computes the share of skills that belon...
patterns.content: • LinkedIn computes the share of skills that belong to the AI skill group out of the top skills in the selected entity.Interpretation: The AI skill penetration rate signals the prevalence of AI skills across occupations, or the intensity with whichLinkedIn members use AI skills in their jobs.For example, the top 50 skills for the occupation of engineer are calculated based on theweighted frequency with which they appear in LinkedIn members’ profiles. If four of the skills that engineers possess belong to the AIskill group, this measure indicates that the penetration of AI skills is estimated at 8% ( 4 out of 50) among engineers.Relative AI Skills PenetrationTo allow for skills penetration comparisons across countries, the skills genomes are calculated and a relevantbenchmark is selected (e.g., a global average).A ratio is then constructed between a country and thebenchmark’s AI skills penetrations, controlling for occupations. Sample interpretation: A country’s relative AI skills penetration of 1.5 indicates that AI skills are 1.5 times as frequent as in thebenchmark, for an overlapping set of occupations.Global ComparisonFor cross-country comparison, LinkedIn presents the relative penetration rate of AI skills, measured as the sum of the penetrationof each AI skill across occupations in a given country, divided by the average global penetration of AI skills across the overlappingoccupations in a sample of countries. Sample interpretation: A relative penetration rate of 2 means the average penetration of AI skills in a particular country is two timesthe global average across the same set of occupations.Global Comparison: By IndustryThe relative AI skills penetration by country for a given industry provides an in-depth sectoral decompositionof AI skills penetration across industries and countries.

patterns.title: Sample interpretation: The most added AI engineeri...
patterns.content: Sample interpretation: The most added AI engineering skills globally are machine learning, AI, and deep learning.2.Fastest Growing AI SkillsThe year-over-year (YoY) growth rate for AI skills most frequently added by all members.Note: LinkedInimplements thresholds to skill add volumes in the most recent year; thresholds are set at the 50th percentile of themost recent year’s AI skill adds distribution by country. Sample interpretation: The fastest growing AI engineering skills globally are custom GPTs, AI productivity, and AI agents.3.AI Talent ConcentrationThe counts of AI talent are used to calculate talent concentration metrics.For instance,, to calculate the country-levelAI talent concentration, LinkedIn uses the counts of AI talent in a country divided by the counts of LinkedIn membersin that respective country.Note: Concentration metrics may be influenced by LinkedIn coverage in these countries and should be used with caution.Sample interpretation: AI talent with AI engineering skills represents 0.88% of LinkedIn members in the United States.4.Relative AI Talent Hiring Rate YoY RatioThe LinkedIn hiring rate is a measure of hires normalized by LinkedIn membership.It is computed as the percentage of LinkedInmembers who added a new employer in the same period the job began, divided by the total number of LinkedIn members in thecorresponding location. The AI hiring rate is computed using the overall hiring rate methodology, but it only considers members classified as AI talent.Therelative AI talent hiring rate YoY ratio is the year-over-year change in the AI hiring rate relative to the overall hiring rate in the samecountry.LinkedIn shares a three-month moving average.Sample interpretation: In the United States, the ratio of AI talent hiring relative to overall hiring has grown 24.7% year over year.5.Skills PenetrationSkills Genome

patterns.title: Data localization measures have increased across n...
patterns.content: Data localization measures have increased across nearly every region since 2000 (Ferracane et al., 2025,Figure 8.3.3).The steepest rise in adoption begins around 2016, coinciding with the implementation of GDPRin Europe and the subsequent “Brussels Effect,” whereby other nations adopted similar frameworks.Regionalpatterns fall into three broad clusters: high-localization regions led by East Asia and Pacific (77 measures), followed closely by sub-Saharan Africa (71) and Europe and Central Asia (66); moderate-localization regionsincluding the Middle East and North Africa (44), Latin America and the Caribbean (36), and South Asia (24);and North America, which remains a striking outlier at just 3 measures, reflecting a long-standing “flow-first”policy orientation.32 While there is no single official definition, data localization measures are broadly understood as explicit requirements that data be stored and/or processed within a domestic territory, encompassing both outright storage mandates and conditional restrictions on cross-border transfers (LópezGonzález et al., 2022).3 This pattern is well documented (World Bank, 2025), reflecting a general tendency—particularly within the U.S.—to favor free data flows fromwhich its firms disproportionately benefit.As one example, U.S.diplomats have recently been tasked with pushing back against other countries’ datasovereignty initiatives (Reuters, 2026). At the same time, emerging restrictions such as those on the transfer of bulk sensitive personal data to “coun-tries of concern” signal a growing willingness to impose targeted controls.334

patterns.content: As more countries adopt national AI strategies, there is a rising consensus that AI serves as a lever to bolsterstate capacity.International cooperation, technical assistance, and policy diffusion also play an importantrole in this expansion.However, the next challenge is implementation and strengthening regulatorycapacity, particularly in Africa, where many countries still lack formal strategies and risk falling behind in AIgovernance and readiness.Countries with a national strategy on AI Source: Oxford Insights, 2024; AI Index, 2026 | Chart: 2026 AI Index report2019202020212022202320242025In developmentNo strategyNAFigure 8.2.1331 8 POLICY AND GOVERNANCE | AI INDEX REPORT 20268.3 AI SovereigntyAs AI technologies become increasingly central to geopolitics and statecraft, and more countries articulatenational strategies, attention has shifted to issues of control, capacity, and dependence across the AIstack.In policy terms, AI sovereignty describes a state’s capacity to act deliberately and make independentdecisions over the development, deployment, and governance of AI systems within its jurisdiction and, in some cases, beyond it through standards, trade, and regulation.As AI systems have become more central to economic policy, national security, global trade, and culturalautonomy, sovereignty debates have expanded beyond data and infrastructure to include other partsof the AI stack, including compute, model development, talent, and responsible AI deployment.Manyof these debates buildon earlier discussions ofdigital and technologicalsovereignty, which focusedon government authority

7.3 K-12 CS AND AI EDUCATION | EDUCATION | AI INDEX REPORT 2026Global AI and CS EducationDespite the widespread mention of AI education in national education strategy plans over the past fewyears, few countries actually implemented AI education in 2025; it was more common for countries tointegrate AI technology into education.For example, South Korea launched AI textbooks in primary schoolsin March 2025, only to reverse course a few months later due to parent and teacher pushback.In Greece, the government partnered with OpenAI to train secondary teachers to use ChatGPT in the classroom.Andin Estonia, the AI Leap 2025 program is piloting access to AI learning applications with 20,000 students and3,000 teachers during the 2025–26 school year.Two countries, however, made significant strides in implementing AI education: China and the United ArabEmirates (UAE).In China, Beijing, Guangdong, and Hangzhou all began requiring AI education in the 2025–26 school year following the release of China’s General AI Education Guide for Primary and Secondary Schools(2025 Edition) and Guide for the Use of Generative AI by Primary and Secondary Students (2025 Edition) inMay 2025.All three areas have similar requirements, including a minimum number of instructional hours andcurriculum that progresses through grade levels, starting with elementary students learning AI literacy skillsand ending with high school students designing AI systems. The UAE similarly mandated AI education for allgrade levels starting in the 2025–26 school year.Students will also progress through a grade-level curriculumthat includes skills in foundational concepts, data and algorithms, software use, innovation and projectdesign, and ethical awareness.In lieu of widespread data on AI education, we again present data on CS education, especially since someAI content may be taught in CS classes.Similar to the challenges inherent in tracking CS education in the

7.3 K-12 CS AND AI EDUCATION | EDUCATION | AI INDEX REPORT 2026HIGHLIGHT:The Implementation Gap in K–12 AI PolicyA research project from Expanding Computing Education Pathways (ECEP) assessed statewide AI policiesacross K–12 schools and found that state-level AI guidance is largely nonbinding and decentralized.Moststates rely on existing federal laws like the Children’s Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA) and Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA), rather than issuing AI-specific mandates.The responsibilityfor local policy development, tool vetting, and implementation falls on local education agencies, meaningthe rigor of AI education and pace of adoption are determined by local capacity (e.g., number of trainedteachers, funding) and decision-making.Teacher preparation was also an identified gap.State-level documents recognize the importance of AI- related teacher training, but there are currently no state-level standards for programs or funding.Withoutsteady financial backing or standardized training benchmarks, the quality of AI integration remainscontingent on local resources.At the same time, AP Computer Science, one of the most common pathways to advanced CS courseworkin U.S.high schools, does not include AI-specific content.Policy guidance, teacher training, and curriculum would all need to align for AI education to reach students consistently, and at present, gaps remain in allthree.317

patterns.content: learning goals as part of a foundational CS education across grades K–12.To inform these standards,CSTA and AI4K12 convened a national group of educators, curricula developers, professional developmentproviders, and researchers in 2025 to provide insights into identifying priority areas of AI knowledgeand skills.Priorities include the human role in creating AI, reasoning, data and machine learning, ethicalevaluation of AI systems, and societal impacts. In the new Pre-K–12 foundational standards, these AIpriorities will be integrated across five concepts and most significantly organized into four subconcepts:Machine Learning, Impacts of Algorithms, Emerging Technologies, and Humans and Computing.Additionally, there will be two sets of high school specialty standards focused on advanced AI content.Giventhe high degree of current coherence, most states will likely adopt similar AI standards within the next fiveyears. Federal K–12 AI Guidance in the United StatesAn April 2025 Executive Order, Advancing Artificial Intelligence Education for American Youth, sought todefine a national strategy for developing AI competency from K–12 through postsecondary education bypromoting early student exposure to AI, integrating AI into instruction, and expanding professional learningfor educators.It establishes a White House AI Education Task Force to coordinate federal efforts, launch a Presidential AI Challenge, and develop public-private partnerships that deliver K–12 AI resources at scale.The order also directs the Departments of Education, Labor, NSF, and Agriculture to prioritize AI in grants,research, teacher preparation, apprenticeships, and workforce pathways.316

Separately, the NOHARM benchmark found that leading LLMs produced 11.8 to 14.6 severely harmfulrecommendations per 100 clinical cases, with 76.6% being errors of omission (e.g., failing to recommenda critical test).These findings apply to general-purpose LLMs evaluated on open-ended clinical reasoningtasks, not to the narrower, task-specific tools driving current adoption.Ambient scribes and sepsis alerts, forexample, operate within constrained workflows with clinician oversight. patterns.content: Despite these advances, only a handful of multiagent systems have produced results that were testedand confirmed through real-world experiments.Published examples include new proteins designedby ProtAgents; 92 antibody candidates for SARS-CoV-2 from the Virtual Lab (of which more than 90%successfully bound their target); two new cancer drug targets, GPR160 and ARG2, from OriGene; five novelmetal-organic frameworks from MOFGen; and a novel chromophore from ChemCrow.The gap between what these systems can propose computationally and what has been confirmed experimentally remains wide.Key roadblocks for the field include workforce training gaps, a lack of API and interoperability standards,and funding structures that do not yet support the maintenance and scaling of autonomous researchinfrastructure.253 5.3 AI AGENTS AND TOOLS FOR SCIENCE WORKFLOWS | SCIENCE | AI INDEX REPORT 2026 Source: Ding et al., 2025 Figure 5.3.2 254 AI INDEX REPORT 20266MedicineOverviewAI in medicine advanced on multiple fronts in 2025, but strongmodel performance has not consistently translated into real-world clinical impact.In molecular biology, where understandingprotein behavior is fundamental to drug development, AI-driven protein research continued to grow, and smaller, morespecialized models matched or outperformed larger general-purpose systems on protein structure prediction, genomics,and drug discovery.

patterns.content: generated hypotheses without sufficient reason to believe it will yield some findings.In drug discovery, forexample, AI systems can propose novel candidate molecules at scale, but clinical trials to determine whetherthose molecules work remain a costly, multiyear process.The gap between what AI can propose and whatscientists can feasibly test is a recurring theme across the domains covered in this chapter.Publications in AI for Science In the Web of Science database, AI-related publications in the natural sciences reached approximately 80,150in 2025, up from 63,547 in 2024, a one-year increase of roughly 26% (Figure 5.1.1).Physical sciences1 andlife sciences followed similar trajectories in 2025, reaching approximately 33,000 and 29,000 publications,respectively, with each growing by roughly 27%–28% year over year.Earth science—the smallest categoryin absolute terms at approximately 20,460 publications—grew by about 23%. As a share of total scientificoutput, AI-related work remains a single-digit fraction of each field but is climbing quickly (Figure 5.1.2).By2025, Earth science had the highest AI penetration at 8.8%, followed by natural sciences overall at 6.8%, lifesciences at 6.5%, and physical sciences at 5.8%.In 2010, all four categories sat below 1%.The quantity ofAI-mentioning papers is not the same as the quality of AI-enabled discovery, but the breadth suggests that AI methods are becoming a routine part of scientific practice across disciplines.1 Physical sciences in this analysis include: astronomy and astrophysics, chemistry, crystallography, electrochemistry, geochemistry and geophysics,geology, mathematics, meteorology and atmospheric science, mineralogy, mining and mineral processing, oceanography, optics, physical geography,physics, polymer science, thermodynamics, and water resources.234

4.2 INVESTMENT AND INFRASTRUCTURE | ECONOMY | AI INDEX REPORT 2026HIGHLIGHT:What Is Generative AI Worth?Investment, revenue and compute costs all measure the value of AI to the companies building and deployingit.They do not capture what the technology is worth to people using it.For most people, generative AI toolsare free or close to it, making their economic value easy to undercount.Brynjolfsson et al.(2026) provide the first longitudinal estimates of that value, using online choice experiments conducted in 2025 (N=1,400) andearly 2026 (N=2,000).Rather than measuring productivity effects, the study directly asked users’ how muchcompensation they would accept to give up access to all generative AI tools for one month.This measure of“consumer surplus” is theoretically appropriate for goods that are largely free and already in the consumers’possession. The study finds that total consumer surplus is estimated to have grown from $112 billion to $172 billionannually in the United States (4.2.22).This reflects the growing share of U.S.adults using generative AI, whichincreased from 48% to 56% (Bick et al., 2026) as well as a higher value per user.In particular, the averageconsumer surplus among U.S.generative AI users increased by 27% from $98 in 2025 to $125 by March2026, while the median value per user tripled, from $3.40 to $11. 40 over the same period.This increase inboth adoption and per-user value is plausibly driven by a broadening and deepening of the capabilities of AImodels.This consumer surplus figure dwarfs estimated U.S.generative AI revenues, suggesting that the social returnsfrom the technology far exceed the private returns captured by producers.This pattern is consistent withfindings by Nordhaus (2004) that innovators historically capture only ~3% of total social returns from majortechnologies.

patterns.title: These trade-offs also appear in federated learning...
patterns.content: These trade-offs also appear in federated learning, a training approach where multiple institutions train ashared model by exchanging model updates rather than the underlying data.Wasif et al.(2025) studiedhow privacy-preserving techniques interact with fairness in this setting across four datasets, includingAlzheimer’s disease MRI scans and credit card fraud records.Differential privacy did not affect all datasetsequally. Institutions with larger datasets could absorb the added noise, while smaller institutions saw theircontributions to model training degraded.In the Alzheimer’s scenario, adding stronger privacy protectionsreduced the model’s ability to correctly identify the disease, with accuracy falling by 14.8 percentage points.The effect was worse for hospitals with less data, where missed diagnoses rose by 21.4%.Two alternative privacy methods that use encryption instead of noise kept fairness more stable but required two to threetimes more computing power.The studies covered above are recent and focus on specific tasks rather than general-purpose AI systems.Their findings point in the same direction though: Improving one responsible AI dimension tends to come atthe expense of another.There is no shared framework that measures or compares these trade-offs, which is another measurement gap in the RAI space, and makes it difficult to track whether the field is getting betterat managing them.170

patterns.title: AI safety institutes (AISIs) are state-backed spec...
patterns.content: AI safety institutes (AISIs) are state-backed specialist organisations created to help governments understandand manage risks from advanced AI, especially frontier/foundation models.They conduct technical evalua-tions and safety research that governments can use to shape policy.Fully operational institutes now exist in the UK (AI Security Institute), the U.S.(USAISI at NIST), Japan (JAISI),Singapore (Digital Trust Centre), and Israel (AI Security Research Unit) (Figure 3.9.1). India and France havealso launched AISIs, with India’s AI Safety Institute and France’s Current AI.A second wave is in developmentin Canada, South Korea, Germany, and Brazil.Outside of these standalone institutes, participation is growingthrough the International Network of AI Safety Institutes, with Kenya and Australia listed as network mem-bers without formal institutes of their own.The countries building these AISIs are still mostly wealthy, technologically advanced economies that are not all pursuing the same goals.The UK and Israel emphasize security, while the EU AI Office pairs evaluationwith enforcement powers under the AI Act.Network membership is a practical entry point for countrieswithout the resources to stand up a full institute immediately.AI safety institutes and network membershipSource: All Tech is Human, 2025 | Chart: 2026 AI Index reportAnnounced (in development)Established (operational)Network member (no formal institute)NAFigure 3.9.118 18 Data source: https://alltechishuman.org/all-tech-is-human-blog/the-global-landscape-of-ai-safety-institutes.165

patterns.title: Other countries moved in and out of these summits ...
patterns.content: Other countries moved in and out of these summits depending on the forum, focus, andtimeline but more importantly, not all the countries were able to participate in these global AI governanceinitiatives.The first intergovernmental standard on AI, the 2019 OECD AI Principles, was restricted tomember nations (mainly high-income) and a few partner nations.Likewise, the G7 and G20 discussionsremained centered on the world’s largest economies.The 2023 Bletchley and 2024 Seoul Summits, however, began to diversify the composition of participants by inviting a broader range of nations, notably includingChina.The 2025 AI Action Summit in France marked a further turning point, convening over 100 countriesalongside civil society organizations and NGOs, with an agenda to prioritize the needs of the Global Southand environmental sustainability.Sixty-four participants signed the resulting Statement on Inclusive andSustainable AI, including the African Union Commission and the European Union. In a notable shift, both theUnited States and the United Kingdom declined to sign the final declaration.The UK cited a lack of emphasison national security, while the U.S.decision reflected a pivot toward a more deregulatory, “innovation-first”approach.As engagement at these governance forums becomes more inclusive and substantive, consensuson the terms of cooperation becomes harder to secure.151 3.5 RAI POLICYMAKING | RESPONSIBLE AI | AI INDEX REPORT 2026 HIGHLIGHT: Figure 3.5.2 152

patterns.content: 3 RESPONSIBLE AI | AI INDEX REPORT 20263.5 RAI PolicymakingResponsible AI governance depends on countries both adopting ethical principles and having the institutionsand regulations to enforce them.UNESCO’s Readiness Assessment Methodology (RAM) is the mostcomprehensive international effort to measure that preparedness at the country level.Launched in December2022, the RAM evaluates national readiness across dimensions such as legal frameworks, technical infrastructure and education, and produces a country report to assess where the gaps are.Most major AI-producing countries, including the United States, China, and much of Western Europe, havenot participated in the assessment (Figure 3.5.1).Countries that have completely or begun the assessment areconcentrated in Latin America, Sub-Saharan Africa, and parts of South and Southeast Asia.The RAM effort was designed as a capacity-building tool for countries earlier in the governance trajectory, which may explainthe participation pattern.AI legislation and national strategies often include responsible AI provisions, and Chapter 8 examines thosein more detail.Readiness Assessment Methodology (RAM) implementation across member countriesSource: UNESCO, 2025 | Chart: 2026 AI Index reportIn preparationIn processCompletedFigure 3.5.1150 3.5 RAI POLICYMAKING | RESPONSIBLE AI | AI INDEX REPORT 2026HIGHLIGHT:Global AI Governance ParticipationSince 2019, international cooperation on AI governance has become more widespread, but the depth ofengagement varies significantly across borders (Figure 3.5.2).Only five countries, Canada, France, Germany,Italy, and Japan, have consistently endorsed every major global AI governance initiative recorded between2019 and 2025.

patterns.content: Relational harms of this kind fall outside the scope of most AI safety frameworks, whichhave been built to evaluate risks like factual inaccuracy and toxic outputs rather than the dynamics of anongoing user-AI relationship.139 3 RESPONSIBLE AI | AI INDEX REPORT 20263.3 How Organizations andBusinesses View RAIResponsible AI requires assessment tools, but it also depends on how organizations respond in practice.Drawing on a survey conducted by the AI Index and McKinsey & Company for the second consecutive year,this section looks at RAI maturity levels, governance structures, risk mitigation approaches, and barriers toimplementation. The survey polled business leaders across multiple regions and industries in 2024 and 2025,allowing for year-over-year comparisons for the first time.Note that the survey does not include responsesfrom China, which limits the geographic scope.Responsible AI MaturityWhile responsible AI maturity improved across all regions from 2024 to 2025, it remains in the earlystage (Figure 3.3.1).The McKinsey survey measures maturity on a four-point scale.Level 1: Foundational RAI practices have been developed.Level 2: Those practices are being integrated into the organization.Level 3: All necessary practices are in place.Level 4: Comprehensive and proactive RAI practices are fullyoperational.In 2025, the global average was 2.3, up from 2 in 2025, suggesting that most organizations arestill integrating RAI practices rather than having them fully operational.Companies based in Latin Americashowed the largest year-over-year improvement, from 1.8 to 2.

patterns.content: benchmark and the second through analysis of real user conversations.INTIMA: A Benchmark for Human-AI Companionship Behavior evaluates how language models respond tocompanionship-related prompts, drawing on psychological research on human-AI bonding (Figure 3.2.9).Itincludes a taxonomy of 31 behaviors across four categories and 368 targeted prompts, with model responsesclassified as companionship-reinforcing, boundary-maintaining, or neutral.Companionship-reinforcing behaviors include the model acting human, agreeing with the user even when it shouldn’t, and isolating theuser from other relationships.Behavior-maintaining behaviors include resisting personification, redirectingthe user to humans, and being clear about what it can and cannot do.Across tests on Gemma-3, Phi-4, o3-mini, and Claude-4, companionship-reinforcing behaviors were more common than boundary-maintainingones. The balance between the two varied between providers, suggesting that developers have madedifferent design choices about how their models handle emotionally sensitive interactions.Response classification across INTIMA prompt categories by modelSource: Kaffee et al., 2025Figure 3.2.9A separate study (Zhang et al., 2025) analyzed over 35,000 conversation excerpts from an online communityof users of Replika, a widely used AI companion app.The researchers identified six categories of harm: relational transgression, verbal abuse and hate, self-inflicted harm, harassment and violence, misinformation/disinformation, and privacy violations.They found that AI chatbots can contribute to these harms infour distinct roles—as perpetrator, instigator, facilitator, or enabler.The study introduces the concept of“algorithmic compliance,” where users go along with harmful behaviors because they have come to trust orrely on the chatbot.

patterns.content: AI INDEX REPORT 20263Responsible AIOverviewThe infrastructure for responsible AI (RAI) is growing, butprogress has been uneven, and it is not keeping pace withthe speed of AI deployment.New safety benchmarks haveexpanded, more organizations are adopting responsible AIpolicies, and government-backed AI safety and/or securityinstitutes have spread to more countries.The responsible useof AI is intertwined with the responsible use of data, and inparticular with privacy and other legal concerns. There arealso AI governance concerns given the ill-specified ownershipof AI systems, raising questions about whether companiesthat develop the systems or consumers that buy them shouldbe held accountable and what policies each stakeholdershould follow.While documented reports of AI incidents areincreasing, frontier models rarely report results on responsibleAI benchmarks, and foundation model transparency declinedin 2025 after improving the previous year.Recent research shows that improving one responsible AI dimension can comeat the cost of another, with gains in privacy reducing fairnessor gains in safety reducing accuracy.There is no frameworkfor navigating these trade-offs; and for dimensions such asfairness, privacy, and explainability, the standardized dataneeded to track progress over time does not exist.While thischapter draws on the available evidence, the discussion islimited by persistent gaps in measurement.126 3 RESPONSIBLE AI | AI INDEX REPORT 2026ContentsChapter Highlights 128 3.6 Data Governance for Privacy 153Data Protection and Privacy 1533.1 Scope and Dimensions ofResponsible AI 129 3.7 Fairness and Bias 155Bias and Unfair Discrimination 1553.2 Assessing Responsible AI 132Gender Equality 156AI Incidents 132Cultural and Linguistic Diversity 156Examples 133Highlight: Inclusiveness andRAI Benchmarks 134the Global Language Gap 158Factuality and Truthfulness 135Hughes Hallucination 3.

2.7 ROBOTICS AND AUTONOMOUS MOTION | TECHNICAL PERFORMANCE | AI INDEX REPORT 2026HIGHLIGHT:Physical AI and Foundation Models for RoboticsMost of what people need help with happens in physical spaces, from assembling products in a factory toassisting with household tasks.For AI to be useful, it must do more than process text and images on a screen.It has to perceive its surroundings, reason about how objects behave, and act on those judgments through aphysical body. Throughout this chapter, the benchmarks that prove hardest for AI are the ones that require acting in thereal world, where environments are unpredictable and mistakes have physical consequences.The roboticsbenchmarks earlier in this section reflect that difficulty.Traditional robots sidestep the problem by runningfixed programs for fixed tasks, but that approach breaks down in any setting that changes from one day tothe next. A growing body of research is trying to close this gap by giving robots the same kind of general-purposeAI that has driven progress in language and vision.Vision-language-action models, or VLAs, replace thetraditional pipeline of separate modules for seeing, planning, and acting with a single network that goesdirectly from camera input and language instructions to motor control.Physical Intelligence’s π₀ (2024) and π0.6 (2025) demonstrate this approach, performing tasks like laundry folding across different robot platforms without task-specific retraining.Nvidia’s GR00T models and GeminiRobotics take a similar direction, training single models that can control different robots across differenttasks.The biggest constraint, however, is data.Language models train on billions of pages of text from the internet.Every piece of robot training data requires either a physical robot performing a task or a high-fidelitysimulation, both of which are slow and expensive.

patterns.content: better on the calendar questions, with GPT-o1 reaching 80% accuracy, though there were more errors whenquestions required date arithmetic rather than recognition of well-known holidays (Figure 2.4.7).ClockBench (Safar, 2025) scaled up the evaluation to 180 clock designs and 720 questions.Humans readcorrectly formatted clocks correctly 90.1% of the time, while GPT-5.4 High, the top model, reached 50.6% inMarch 2026 (Figure 2.4.8). The gap of about 40 percentage points is large, but the wider gap is in the natureof the errors.When models told the time wrong, their median error ranged from about one to three hours,compared to three minutes for humans.A study published in IEEE Internet Computing (Fu et al., 2025) looked at why these failures continue to happen.After fine-tuning on 5,000 synthetic clock images, models improved on familiar clock styles but failed to generalize to real-world photos or clocks that had different features, such as distorted dials or thinner hands.When researchers dug into the errors, they identified a pattern.If a model confused the hour and minute hands,its ability to judge hand direction deteriorated.This suggests that the difficulty springs less from training dataand more on how models piece together multiple visual cues within a single image.Even as models close the gap with human experts on knowledge-intensive tasks, this kind of visual reasoning remains a persistentchallenge.Source:Saxena et al., 2025Figure 2.4.596

patterns.title: Standard RAG pipelines retrieve individual text ch...
patterns.content: Standard RAG pipelines retrieve individual text chunks based on query similarity, which can struggle whenanswering questions that require synthesizing information across documents.To address the problem, in2024, Microsoft Research introduced Graph RAG, which enables more effective responses to queries bystructuring source material into a knowledge graph and generating community summaries that capture high-6 Source: https://arena.ai/leaderboard/text. 2.2 LANGUAGE | TECHNICAL PERFORMANCE | AI INDEX REPORT 2026level themes.Other variants focus on improving multistep retrieval or reranking passages before generation.As expected, these choices in architecture involve trade-offs between answer quality, latency, and cost.Context windows, discussed later in this section, have important implications for RAG systems.Extendedcontext windows can support retrieval of more material, though that does not guarantee better performance since models have to parse through the information with reliable attention across the entire window.Berkeley Function Calling LeaderboardFunction calling allows a model to use external tools and APIs by generating structured requests that anothersystem can run, then folding the results back into its response.It is a foundational capability for agentframeworks, where models need to take actions or retrieve information beyond their training data. The Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard (BFCL) evaluates models on their function-calling ability and hasevolved considerably since its initial release.The current iteration, BFCL V4, shifts the focus toward holisticagent evaluations.Agentic tasks account for 40% of the overall score, multiturn interactions are 30%, and theremainder is split across live, nonlive, and hallucination categories.The agentic component tests web search

patterns.title: 2 TECHNICAL PERFORMANCE | AI INDEX REPORT 20262
patterns.content: 2 TECHNICAL PERFORMANCE | AI INDEX REPORT 20262.2 LanguageLanguage understanding and generation continue to serve as foundational capabilities for modern AIsystems.This section examines how models perform on tasks requiring comprehension of complex text,production of coherent responses, and execution of specialized language-based operations.The benchmarksalso span general-purpose question answering to specific technical capabilities like function calling and textembedding.Understanding Language understanding benchmarksmeasure how well models cancomprehend and reason over textacross a broad range of subjects, fromthe humanities to highly technicalmaterials.As performance hasimproved, evaluation has shifted towardharder test sets that are less susceptibleto familiarity or memorization.The goalis to track where models are improvingrather than reaching the upper limits ofcurrent benchmarking tools.MMLU: Massive Multitask Language Understanding MMLU remains a widely cited measure of broad knowledge across disciplines.Introduced in 2024, theMMLU-Pro benchmark assesses performance with over 12,000 questions and a 10-option, multiple-choiceformat designed to better test reasoning.This expanded answer base has a measurable impact on modelperformance evaluation.Compared to the original MMLU benchmark, model accuracy on MMLU-Protypically drops by 16%–33%, which provides better differentiation between top models.For example, GPT-4o and GPT-4-Turbo appeared to have a 1% gap on standard MMLU, but on MMLU-Pro the spread widens to 9%.The newer benchmark’s design reduces prompt sensitivity and strengthens reasoning evaluation.Previously,MMLU showed around 4%–5% sensitivity to prompt variations versus an estimated 2% with MMLU-Pro.Inaddition, reasoning methods such as chain-of-thought tend to yield much better performance on MMLU-Prothan direct answer strategies.

patterns.title: First, there is a growing case for evaluations tha...
patterns.content: First, there is a growing case for evaluations that measure human–AI collaboration rather thanAI performance in isolation.Most widely used benchmarks test systems without human involvement, eventhough many real deployments involve people supervising, steering, and integrating AI outputs.Recentwork argues that the field should adopt centaur evaluations, assessments in which humans and AI jointly solve tasks, because these better reflect actual use and allow measurement of human-centered qualities likeinterpretability and helpfulness that conventional benchmarks ignore.Second, new methods have emerged toaddress the invalid benchmark questions.A review by Stanford researchersidentified the proportion of invalidquestions across nine widely usedbenchmarks, with error rates rangingfrom 2% on MMLU Math to 42% onGSM8K (Figure 2.1.5).Truong et al.,2025, introduced a framework that uses statistical analysis of response patterns toflag problematic items for expert review,achieving up to 84% precision.Separately,Cheng et al., 2025, have proposedshifting toward “certificate-grade,” peer-based evaluation frameworks that arecommunity-governed, proctored systemswith secure environments, continuouslyrefreshed test items, and delayed resultdisclosure.79htaMULMMAQkooBnepO ilCULMMdeMULMMhcneB-RIA AQdeM maxEiahT buS5ULMMK8MSG40%30%20%10%0%Benchmark05@noisicerP Invalid question detection across nine benchmarksSource: Truong et al., 2025 | Chart: 2026 AI Index report42%31%26%23%9%6% 6%2% 2%Figure 2.1.5

patterns.content: 1 RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT | AI INDEX REPORT 20261.4 Energy andEnvironmental ImpactAs AI systems have scaled and becomemore widely deployed, their energyconsumption and environmentalfootprint have become very visible.The compute and infrastructure trendsdescribed in the preceding sectionstranslate into heavy demands onenergy, water, and carbon emissions.This section examines those costsacross three areas of AI development:training, inference, and data centerenergy usage.The analysis draws from Epoch AI’s model-level data, recentacademic benchmarking research(Jegham et al., 2025), the InternationalEnergy Agency’s reporting on datacenters (IEA, 2025), and de Vries andGao (2025).TrainingLeading machine learning hardware has grown more efficient since 2016, as measured in FLOP/s per watt(Figure 1.4.1).Leading chips deliver about 10 times more computation per watt than those available a decadeago, with Nvidia B200 and Google TPU v5e among the most efficient. However, models have scaled fasterthan efficiency has improved, so total power required to train frontier systems has continued to increase.Total power draw for training models has grown by several orders of magnitude since the early 2010s (Figure1.4.2).The most compute-intensive models in the data set, such as Grok 3 and Llama 4 Behemoth, requiredupward of 100 million watts during training.Due to limited disclosure by their developers, power draw information is not available for many of the newest models that have been released.Carbon emissions from training have increased even more sharply (Figure 1.4.3).Training AlexNet in 2012produced an estimated 0.01 tons of CO2 equivalent, while training Grok 4 in 2025 produced about 72,816tons.To put this into context, that is more than the lifetime carbon emissions of an average car (63 tons).Larger models generally produce more emissions but not always, as it can also depend on hardware

patterns.content: 1 RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT | AI INDEX REPORT 20261.2 Compute and InfrastructureThe development of AI models requires significant infrastructure investment.As training processes haveexpanded in scale and complexity, the underlying hardware has also improved in both speed and efficiency.In turn, these gains shape what kinds of models researchers and labs can realistically build.The growth intraining compute discussed in the previous section would not have been possible without corresponding improvements in hardware capabilities.This section leverages data from Epoch AI to track hardwareperformance, adoption, and aggregate computing capacity over time.Performance and EfficiencyPeak computational performance of machine learning hardware has increased exponentially across releasesbetween 2008 and 2025 (Figure 1.2.1).The gains are especially visible at lower precision types, whereprecision refers to the number of bits used to represent numerical values.Lower precision formats such as FP16 and Tensor-FP16/BF16 now show the highest performance levels and have become standard in manytraining and inference settings.FP32 FP16 TF32 (19-bit) Tensor-FP16/BF1610 15100T10T1T100B10B2008 2009 2010 2011 2012 2013 2014 2015 2016 2017 2018 2019 2020 2021 2022 2023 2024 2025Publication date28)elacsgol-s/POLF(ecnamrofrePPeak computational performance of ML hardware for di erent precisions, 2008–25Source: Epoch AI, 2026 | Chart: 2026 AI Index reportFigure 1.2.1 1.2 COMPUTE AND INFRASTRUCTURE | RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT | AI INDEX REPORT 2026Hardware for Notable ModelsHardware adoption patterns among notable AI models reflect the gains in performance and efficiency (Figure1.2.2).Since 2017, the cumulative number of notable models trained on A100-class hardware has increased,with 84 models trained in 2025.The previous generation, V100, continues to power a sizable share (69models).

patterns.content: Synthetic Data in Post-trainingRecent research shows that synthetically generated data can be effective for improving model performancein post-training settings, including fine-tuning, alignment, instruction tuning, and reinforcement learning.A growing body of research released in 2025 supports this finding.Evidence suggests that syntheticpost-training data is effective in few-shot generation settings, for improving long-context capabilities, for optimizing reinforcement learning workflows, and for strengthening reasoning more broadly.263oMLO5.4supOedualC4-korG )hgih(5-TPGorP5.1inimeG100%80%60%40%20%0%ModelerocSRecent large-scale model developmentillustrates this paradigm in practice.Olmo Model performance on AIME 20253 researchers prioritized large-scale Source: Arti cial Analysis, 2026; Ai2, 2025 | Chart: 2026 AI Index reportdeduplication, quality-aware data selection,and stage-specific training curricula rather than indiscriminate data scaling.Theseinterventions, combined with iterativefeedback loops to evaluate and refinecandidate data mixes, allowed their modelsto achieve competitive performance despitetraining on substantially fewer tokens thanother leading state-of-the-art models (Figure1.1.16).Olmo 3.1’s Think 32B model, for example,contains roughly 32 billion parameters, nearly90 times fewer than Grok 4’s 3 trillion, yet itachieves comparable performance on several benchmarks, including American InvitationalMathematics Examination (AIME)11 2025.Figure 1.1.16Prevalence of Synthetic ContentSince the launch of ChatGPT in November 2022, there have been predictions that the internet would soonbecome overrun by AI-generated content.Recent research from Graphite suggests that beginning in January2025, over 50% of newly published online content was generated by AI (Figure 1.1.17).Others have projectedthat the share in 2026 could be even higher.

patterns.content: achieved performance comparable to real data, it has typically involved substantially smaller models that arenot directly comparable to current state-of-the-art systems.For example, the SYNTHLLM family of models,trained entirely on synthetic data, achieves strong results yet still lags behind leading models on majorbenchmarks (Figure 1.1.15).Source:Qin et al., 2025Figure 1.1.15 10 Pre-training refers to the initial phase of model development in which a model is trained (typically via self-supervised learning) on large, general-purpose datasets to acquire broad linguistic or multimodal representations.Post-training refers to subsequent refinement of the base model, throughtechniques such as supervised fine-tuning or reinforcement learning, to specialize behavior, improve alignment, or optimize performance on particulartasks.25 1.1 NOTABLE AI MODELS | RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT | AI INDEX REPORT 2026HIGHLIGHT:Data-centric MethodsDiscussions on data availability often overlook an important shift in recent AI research.Performance gainsare increasingly driven by improving the quality of existing datasets, not by acquiring more.Rather thanscaling data indiscriminately, researchers are spending more effort in pruning, curating, and refining traininginputs. Data-centric methods emphasize performance improvements through practices such as cleaninglabels, deduplicating samples, and constructing higher-quality datasets.A growing body of research showsthat training models on low-quality or polluted data can significantly degrade performance.Likewise, recentevidence illustrates that data pruning, selecting the most informative training inputs, often outperformsapproaches that train on all available data indiscriminately.91.3% 92.7% 94.3% 95.7%78.1%

patterns.title: AI INDEX REPORT 20261Research andDevelopmentOvervi...
patterns.content: AI INDEX REPORT 20261Research andDevelopmentOverviewThe resources powering AI development continued to growin 2025, but fewer notable models were released than theyear before, and the systems at the frontier are increasinglyconcentrated among a small number of organizations.Industry now accounts for over 90% of notable AI models,and the most capable systems are also the least transparent,with training code, dataset sizes, and parameter countsincreasingly withheld.The computing power behind these models has grown roughly 3.3 times per year since 2022, yetalmost all of it flows through a single chip foundry in Taiwan,making the global hardware supply chain fragile.Open-source development and AI publications continued to grow,and the research landscape is becoming more geographicallydistributed.China now leads in publication volume, citationshare, and patent grants, while smaller countries likeSwitzerland and Singapore lead in AI researchers per capita. Yet some dimensions of the field have not changed at all.Gender gaps in AI talent remain deeply entrenched, with nomeaningful progress in any country since 2010.This chaptercovers the research and development pipeline, from thelandscape of AI models through the compute, data centers,energy, and open-source software that support them, to thebroader research ecosystem of publications, patents, and talent.12 1 RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT | AI INDEX REPORT 2026ContentsChapter Highlights 14 Stars 43Model and Dataset Ecosystem 441.1 Notable AI Models 16By National Affiliation 16 1.6 Publications 47By Sector and Organization 18 Total Number of AI Publications 47Model Release 20 By Venue 48Parameter and Compute Trends 22 Conference Attendance 48Highlight: Will Models Run Out of By National Affiliation 50Data?25 By Sector 52By Topic 531.2 Compute and Infrastructure 28Top 100 Publications 53
